analyst_view.overall: Early view: Chelsea have lost four of their 10 league games, the latest 1-0 at Sunderland, and Xabi Alonso said afterwards his side lacked patience and quality in the final third. They are still without Joao Pedro, Reece James, Maxence Lacroix and Jamie Gittens. Leeds come in after beating Tottenham 1-0 with a late Noah Okafor goal.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean lower: Chelsea are missing Joao Pedro, Alonso complained about the final-third quality at Sunderland, and Leeds' last two league games ended 1-0 and 0-2. A tight game looks more likely than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Chelsea will have more of the ball and wide players like Estevao and Neto to win corners, but Leeds kept Tottenham out for 90 minutes last time and are not easy to pin back. I stay close to the site.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards. Chelsea were booked four times at Sunderland, which fits the figure, while Leeds had only two bookings against Tottenham. With no referee named yet, I keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.4 shots, 14 of them Chelsea's. I lean slightly higher: after a defeat that angered Alonso, Chelsea should push hard at Stamford Bridge, and Leeds are likely to let them have the ball and look for chances on the break. Most of the extra volume would come from the home side.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9 shots on target. I lean lower: Chelsea's problem at Sunderland was the quality of their chances rather than the amount of possession, and they are without Joao Pedro. Lots of efforts from outside the box would keep this figure down.
